name: Careers Electric Summer Academy (summer pre-apprenticeship)
sourceWorkbook: Forsyth Tech: the catalog's Programs Offered tables 2021–22 through 2026–27 (D35130, C35130, CIP 46.0302, day; the diploma marked REVISED for 2026–27), the 2025–26 Electrical Systems Technology diploma and certificate pages (term lines and the 39- and 15-credit totals), the program pages (one-year diploma, 1–2-semester certificate, 2100 Silas Creek Pkwy), the 2023 Career & College Promise booklet (C35130P1), the Technical Career Path page, the Careers Electric coverage (WFDD 2026-07-13, NCBCE and EdNC 2026-06), the FCECA apprenticeship page and its published sections, the Workforce Continuing Education catalog page (144 classroom hours a year, 2,000 OJT hours, the NCDOL Journeyman's card), the Installation/Troubleshooting course page, the 2026–27 academic calendar and the course schedule's summer 2026 electrical sections; course hours and credits from the NCCCS Combined Course Library; sequences as the 2025–26 tables give them — compiled 2026-11-18
note: The college's paid seven-week summer academy for high-school students with Winston-Salem/Forsyth County Schools, launched 2026 as one of the NC Business Committee for Education's twelve Careers Electric academies (Siemens Foundation-funded): one or two college electrical courses for credit (not named), industry-valued credentials, hands-on work with local employers, a registered pre-apprenticeship, a $2,000 completion stipend, employer matching afterward and a tuition waiver for those who continue into an apprenticeship; the college says it counts for one year of the four-year electrical apprenticeship. Carried at 144 hours — the standard's minimum for a year's related instruction — because the academy's hours, courses, dates, room and cohort size are not published (statewide, 220 students across twelve academies in 2026). Class size 16 is a stand-in (the college publishes no section cap). Faculty load is the workspace default (16 contact hours of a 40-hour week) — the college publishes no load.
weeklyHoursNote: Term hours per student are the catalog's weekly contact hours × 16 (the 16-week basis), whatever the term's length: the sessions carry them, the posted days, times and rooms place them. Hours and credits are the NCCCS course standard's; every credit course carries its hours with no section on record at the Main Campus (the lab building is not published); the apprenticeship sits on its published evenings at the Strickland Center and the Installation/Troubleshooting course on its published Mon/Wed evenings at West Campus; clinical hours are zero in every course.

courses.title: Careers Electric summer academy (courses not published)
courses.requisites: A Winston-Salem/Forsyth County Schools high-school student
courses.description: Seven weeks of college electrical coursework ("one or two college electrical courses for college credit" — which ones is not published), industry-valued credentials, hands-on work with local employers and a registered pre-apprenticeship, paid, with a $2,000 completion stipend. The college says the academy counts for one year of the four-year electrical apprenticeship; carried here at 144 hours — the US DOL / ApprenticeshipNC minimum for a year's related instruction — because the academy's hours are not published (the model's inference).
